title: CTCF primes repressive chromatin for rapid BRCA1/BARD1 recruitment to drive homologous recombination repair of DNA double-strand breaks.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Ran the cached paper-context tool on the open-access full text (153 kB): the Data Availability Statement says only 'available in the article and in its online supplementary material'. Zero accessions in text, zero text-mined accessions by Europe PMC (hasDbCrossReferences=N, hasTMAccessionNumbers=N), no NCBI links beyond the PMC record itself, and a Zenodo/Dryad search on the DOI returned nothing. Grepped the entire full text for GSE/PXD/SRP/PRJ/BioProject/Zenodo/figshare/GitHub identifiers: no hits at all. The only occurrences of 'ChIP-seq' and 'proteomic' are citations to other people's papers, not data generated here. The Europe PMC supplementaryFiles endpoint timed out twice (60 s and 120 s), so the supplement file itself was not retrievable; however the in-text captions name the entire supplement contents: Supplementary Tables S1-S4 are cloning primer sequences, siRNA knockdown sequences, ChIP-qPCR primers and DNA-end-resection qPCR primers, plus Supplementary Figures S1-S6 (images).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The experimental design and quantification scheme: U2OS-based reporter lines (AsiSI-ER, FokI, DR-GFP, EJ5-GFP) and HEK-293T, read out by immunofluorescence foci counting, co-immunoprecipitation/western blot, ChIP-qPCR at a small number of AsiSI cut sites, and a single resection assay at chromosome position 1:89,458,296 (CCBL2 gene). The Methods state results are 'means +/- standard deviation based on a minimum of three separate replicates' analysed by Student's t-test, i.e. every measurement is summarised in a bar chart rather than released as a table. I could not open the supplement to confirm the absence of a numeric source-data table, but the text never references one.

a1_downloadable.note: FAIL. There is no dataset to download. The Data Availability Statement points only at the article and its supplement; the supplement, per the in-text captions, contains four tables of PCR primer and siRNA oligonucleotide sequences plus six figure panels. No repository deposit anywhere: no Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) series, no Sequence Read Archive (SRA) run, no BioProject, no ProteomeXchange/PRIDE mass-spectrometry accession, no Zenodo/Dryad/figshare record. Europe PMC's own flags confirm no database cross-references and no text-mined accessions. This is a figures-only mechanistic cell-biology paper.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL (not reached, but recorded). Nothing is a column anywhere. The quantities the paper reports - repair-protein focus intensity at breaks, percent single-stranded DNA from resection, homologous-recombination (HR) versus end-joining reporter efficiency - exist only as plotted bar heights in figure images. Any prediction target would have to be reconstructed by digitising graphs from PDF figures, which is exactly the 'label must be constructed' failure.

a3_inputs_present.note: FAIL. There are no per-item feature rows of any kind. The nearest thing to a feature set would be the handful of AsiSI restriction-enzyme cut sites probed by quantitative PCR, but their genomic coordinates are not tabulated in the open text (only one site, chr1:89,458,296, is named) and the primer tables give oligonucleotide sequences, not break-site annotations.

a4_units_stated.note: Not reached. Where quantities are described in Methods they do carry units or a defined scale (percent single-stranded DNA, relative immunoprecipitation by the 2^-ddCt method, fold change), so units are not the problem here - the absence of any tabulated values is.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL. Minimum three biological replicates per condition across roughly six main figures. Even if every bar in every panel were digitised by hand, the result would be on the order of a few hundred condition-level means, far below the ~1,500-row threshold, and they would be means of different assays (microscopy, qPCR, flow-cytometry reporters) that are not mutually comparable.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially fits a laptop, because there is essentially nothing to load.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot be assessed: with no downloadable table there is no count to compare against the paper.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not reached. The underlying measurements are genuine physical assays (antibody staining, quantitative PCR, fluorescent reporter) and are not another model's output, so provenance would have been fine had the values ever been released.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: the paper releases no numeric data, so no model can be trained or evaluated on it.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use chromatin features around a DNA break site to predict whether the cell repairs it by homologous recombination.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would show the model the local chromatin environment of each enzyme-induced DNA double-strand break - histone marks, CTCF (CCCTC-binding factor) occupancy, gene activity, replication timing - in a window around the cut. This paper supplies zero such rows; the number of usable examples here is 0.
plain_idea.predict: How much DNA end resection and homologous-recombination repair happens at that break, which in principle comes from genome-wide end-resection sequencing. In this paper that readout exists only as quantitative-PCR bar charts at a handful of sites, with no coordinates or values released.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Radiation-oncology and PARP-inhibitor groups want to know which breaks in a tumour genome get repaired accurately, which bears on sensitivity to those drugs. But that project would have to be built on the Legube and Nussenzweig labs' deposited break-mapping data, not on this paper.

ml_idea: The only conceivable task - predicting repair-pathway choice at double-strand breaks from local chromatin state - cannot be built from this paper. It would require the genome-wide break-mapping and chromatin datasets already deposited by other groups (for example the AsiSI-induced break maps and histone-modification profiles from the Legube lab, and END-seq from the Nussenzweig lab). This paper adds mechanism and candidate features (CTCF, HP1-gamma, KAP1, SUV39H1, SETDB1, KDM5A, H3K9 methylation, H3K4 demethylation) as biological context, but contributes no rows.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated, because there is no feature or label table to build. The only downloadable artefact is a supplementary PDF of primer and siRNA sequences.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Read the Data Availability Statement and grep the full text for any repository accession. It took one cached tool call and killed the candidate: the statement says 'available in the article and in its online supplementary material' and there are no accessions of any kind.

verdict_reason: Part A1 fails outright: this is a figures-only mechanistic cell-biology paper with no deposited dataset. The Data Availability Statement points at the article itself, there are no GEO/SRA/BioProject/ProteomeXchange/Zenodo accessions anywhere in the text or in Europe PMC's cross-reference and text-mining flags, and the supplement consists of four tables of PCR primer and siRNA sequences plus figure images. A2, A3 and A5 would also fail: every measurement (repair-protein focus intensity, percent single-stranded DNA, homologous-recombination reporter efficiency) exists only as a bar height in a figure, built from a minimum of three replicates per condition, so the label would have to be reconstructed by digitising graphs and would amount to at most a few hundred non-comparable condition means. The underlying biology is interesting and the assays are real measurements, but nothing is machine-readable.
